questions.question: I'm forming a Colorado LLC with two cofounders. Do our names as owners have to appear in the articles of organization we file with the state, and what does the filing actually have to say?

We're setting up a Colorado corporation with three founders and want bare-bones articles of incorporation. If the articles say nothing about cumulative voting, can a minority shareholder pile all of their votes onto one director candidate?

My cofounder and I signed our operating agreement and IP assignment with an e-signature app, never on paper. If a law says documents like these have to be in writing and signed, do the electronic signatures count in Colorado?

A friend and I have been building an app on nights and weekends and splitting the small profit it makes. We never filed anything or signed an agreement. Could Colorado law treat us as partners anyway?

I'm a limited partner in a small Colorado venture fund organized as a limited partnership, not an LLLP. The general partner wants me on the advisory committee to vote on conflict-of-interest deals and on fund borrowing. Would doing that expose me to personal liability for the fund's debts?

A few of us run an unincorporated founders' meetup group in Colorado. We collect dues to cover event costs and don't try to make a profit. If the group signs a venue contract and can't pay, are the members personally on the hook?

It's mid-November and we want our new Colorado LLC to come into existence on January 1 so the first tax year is clean. Can we file the articles now with a later start date, and how far out can that date be?
Our Colorado corporation's articles took effect in March 2026. When is our first periodic report due to the Secretary of State, and how often do we have to file after that?
I'm a solo founder living in Colorado. Can I name myself as my LLC's registered agent at my home address instead of paying a service, and what happens to that if I move out of state?

We're a Delaware corporation based in Texas. Our only ties to Colorado are an account at a Denver bank and a board meeting we hold in a Colorado ski town once a year. Do we have to register with the Colorado Secretary of State as a foreign entity?

Our Delaware company has had customers and staff in Colorado for two years but never registered there. A Colorado customer owes us $40,000. Can we sue in a Colorado court, and are our Colorado contracts still valid?
We missed our periodic report and the Secretary of State now lists our Colorado LLC as delinquent. Does the company still exist, and can we still take a nonpaying client to court?

Our Colorado LLC sat dormant and has been delinquent for about six years, though we never filed anything to dissolve it. What do we have to file to fix its status, and does the long gap change what's required?
We plan to convert our Colorado LLC into a Colorado corporation. Afterward, is it legally a new company? Do the LLC's contracts and debts carry over, or do we have to wind up the LLC first?

Our Colorado LLC has three founding members, and an angel wants to invest $150,000 and become a member. Our operating agreement doesn't cover adding members. Can two of us outvote the third and admit her?
An angel wants 14% annual interest on a convertible note into our Colorado startup. Is there a legal ceiling on the interest rate a written promissory note can carry in Colorado?
Our seed lead wants us to be a Delaware corporation before the round closes. We're a Colorado LLC today. Does Colorado law let the LLC convert directly into a Delaware corporation?
I'm an angel who bought 2% of a Colorado corporation's common stock seven weeks ago. Can I demand to see the board minutes and accounting records now, and what do I have to do to ask?

Our Colorado LLC is manager-managed, and one cofounder is the sole manager. The other members want him replaced, and the operating agreement doesn't say how to remove a manager. What vote does it take?
My cofounder says he's quitting our Colorado LLC as a member next week, even though our operating agreement says members can't withdraw. Can he actually resign, and what can the company do about it?
